result.topic_en: Preparatory computations for an orbit determination from three observations: Gauss eliminates the distances, defines auxiliary coefficients M, M'' and μ, evaluates them numerically with logarithms, and sets up expressions for the chord, the curtate distances ρ, ρ'' and the radii r, r''.

Nun kann man ohne Bedenken setzen $\frac{n''}{n}=\frac{t'-t}{t''-t'}$, $n'=(n+n'')\left(1-\frac{4(t'-t)(t''-t')kk}{(r+r'')^3}\right)$. Wir haben also
$\frac{1}{(r+r'')^3}=\mu+M\varrho+M''\varrho''$ wenn wir setzen
$M=\frac{\sin\beta\left(\frac{\sin(\alpha-P)}{\tang\beta}-\frac{\sin(\alpha'-P)}{\tang\beta'}\right)}{4kkR'\sin(\odot'-P).(t''-t).(t'-t)}$ ; $M''=\frac{\sin\beta''\left(\frac{\sin(\alpha''-P)}{\tang\beta''}-\frac{\sin(\alpha'-P)}{\tang\beta'}\right)}{4kkR'\sin(\odot'-P).(t''-t)(t''-t')}$
$\mu=\frac{-(t''-t')R\sin(\odot-P)+(t''-t)R'\sin(\odot'-P)-(t'-t)R''\sin(\odot''-P)}{4kkR'\sin(\odot'-P).(t''-t)(t'-t)(t''-t')}$
Man kann indessen hier füglich annehmen $\mu=\frac{1}{(R+R'')^3}$ oder $\mu=\frac{1}{8R'^3}$.

methods.what: Linear relation between geocentric distances from three observations (elimination via direction P)
Approximation of triangle-area ratios by time intervals
Linear equation for 1/(r+r'')^3 in the distances with coefficients M, M'', μ
Auxiliary quantities h, H by polar transformation
Expressions for the chord, ρ, ρ'', r, r'' in terms of auxiliary unknown u
Logarithmic numerical evaluation of M, M'', μ, h, H
